decisions.reason: The title incorrectly asserts independence of minors: [2] and [2 0] present Z/2 but have different minor lists. The statement correctly asserts independence of their generated ideal. The finite-free shear comparison and augmentation prove that assertion, and right exact tensoring proves base change. Corrected only the title; no Statement change.

The page explicitly includes lem-internal-hom-fp-qc. Its distinguished-open computation identifies Hom sheaf sections with Hom_A(M,N)_f for finitely presented M, using localisation of Hom; this proves the announced result. The definition itself is the already defined sheaf Hom, so an empty justified_by does not leave its construction unsupported. Left exactness follows by maps into kernels on each open. No repair is warranted.

L3 cites a topological definition for a local-ring assertion. The existing def-residue-field-scheme-point explicitly identifies the maximal ideal with pA_p; corrected L3 and its contract to cite it. Removed the unnecessary unsupported L4 attribution. In k[t]_(t), t/1 is nonzero since k[t] is a domain, and quotienting by t gives k. Thus reduction has a nonzero kernel, as claimed.

The map M to M tensor kappa(p) need not be surjective (Z to Q at (0)). A finite generating list of M does span the fibre over kappa(p), and extracting a basis from that list supplies r global sections. Nakayama makes them generate locally; shrink to a finite-presentation chart. The finite kernel then vanishes after one localisation because its stalk is zero. Rank zero and the dual-number example remain valid.

The right vertical identity had distinct source and target, and the prose assigned the bottom base-change map to the left arrow. Replaced it by kappa_W inverse and labelled the left arrow as affine restriction. Taking W-sections of the restriction comparison followed by kappa_U gives c tensor m mapping to c times m restricted to W, proving the bottom map is an isomorphism and the square commutes. The cover equivalence and all hypotheses are preserved.

F9 omitted the coefficient homomorphism k to S, so its universal quantifier was false. Added that datum and required extension of it; evaluation at (0,0) uses id_k. The minors are xy, x,y,0,0 and 1 in sizes 2,1,0, and the reduced diagonal matrix gives the asserted fibre dimensions. Clarified inherited AC and strengthened the non-local-freeness justification at the origin: nonzero xy annihilates a nonzero stalk over a domain, so that stalk cannot be free.

F5 needs the scheme structure on D(b), while def-affine-scheme-spectrum supplies only topology. Added the existing lem-spectrum-localization-open-immersion, whose proof compares the localisation rings on the basic opens. The pullback comparison is defined via the neighbourhood-colimit map into sheafification; its stalk is the identity on B_q tensor over A_p M_p. Declared the stalkwise isomorphism criterion used at 3.1. The repaired affine-cover theorem still licenses F4 and step 4.1 unchanged.

F5 wrongly used the topological spectrum definition for the affine scheme D(f). Added the existing locally ringed-space localisation isomorphism. At step 4.1, N is over the second chart ring B, so N_f was ill-typed; replaced it by A_f tensor_B N using affine-open restriction. The tensor comparison is the canonical identity on M_p tensor over A_p N_p at each stalk; declared its stalkwise isomorphism criterion. F4 uses only the unchanged cover equivalence of the corrected supplier.

The stated overlap composite was not composable. Corrected it to theta_(Uprime,W)^(-1) after theta_(U,W), which maps Sym_U restricted to W to Sym_Uprime restricted to W. The restriction cocycle then gives compatibility and the triple-overlap identity by cancellation. Added the elementary tensor-quotient universal-property proof of the base-change isomorphism already used in the definition, avoiding reliance on the later consumer lemma. Degree zero, degree one, free modules and Sym(0)=O_X are preserved.

F7 required D(f) as an affine scheme, whereas the principal-localisation corollary states only a homeomorphism. Replaced it by lem-spectrum-localization-open-immersion and its locally ringed-space identification. Noetherian localisations give the required charts; finite local generators descend via a finite distinguished cover. Kernels are finite because they are submodules of finite Noetherian source modules; cokernels and extensions use finite generators. Statement and AC hypothesis remain unchanged.

Balanced additive maps need not be A-bilinear: constant-term extraction on Z[x] gives the rejected counterexample. Replaced the false equivalence by explicit inverse constructions u mapping to (b tensor m mapping to b u(m)) and v mapping to (m mapping to v(1 tensor m)); the first map is B-linear. Corrected the degree-one tensor order and stated overlap agreement for different target charts. The graded algebra isomorphism, restriction compatibility and free polynomial model then follow from the preserved universal property.
